finding.claim: deleteAccount computes canDelete(u, a) but discards the boolean result, so any caller can delete any account by ID, including accounts owned by other users.
finding.source: Path parameter id of DELETE /accounts/{id} (route comment at line 19) plus the caller's User object; assumes the caller is authenticated and the route is wired to this method, which cannot be verified in this file.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) receives attacker-supplied id
Account a = accounts.get(id) loads the victim's account
canDelete(u, a) result discarded; no enforcement

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is logically correct but never enforced; assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) exists and is used correctly by closeAccount (line 29) but not by deleteAccount; no other ownership check on the path. Authentication layer is out of scope and unverified.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) is called at line 22 as a bare statement, so its boolean is discarded. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) would throw, but deleteAccount never calls it; only closeAccount does (line 29). No other ownership check lies between lines 20 and 23.
verdict.reason: deleteAccount at src/AccountService.java:20-23 runs accounts.remove(id) unconditionally after a discarded canDelete(u, a) call at line 22, so any caller of this method can delete any account. The attacker is any authenticated user who can reach the DELETE route, since the route wiring and authentication sit outside this file and cannot be checked here. The flaw itself is confirmed within this file.

finding.claim: For a non-admin caller, a missing account ID yields a NullPointerException while an existing account owned by someone else yields SecurityException, letting an authenticated user enumerate valid account IDs.
finding.source: id parameter of closeAccount (line 27) and deleteAccount (line 20), attacker-controlled by an authenticated non-admin caller.
finding.sink: Differential error response from canDelete/assertCanDelete on a null Account (src/AccountService.java:10, :29)

trace.note: accounts.get(id) returns null for a nonexistent id
a.ownerId() dereferences null for non-admin, throwing NullPointerException; existing foreign account instead throws SecurityException at line 15

finding.guards_checked: Only the u.admin() short-circuit avoids the NPE, and only for admin callers. No null check on Account and no uniform error response.

verdict.guard_found: Only the u.admin() short-circuit in canDelete (src/AccountService.java:10), which skips the null dereference only for admins. There is no null check on the Account from accounts.get at lines 21 and 28. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) throws and nothing catches it, so the NPE-versus-SecurityException difference reaches the caller.
verdict.reason: For a non-admin, closeAccount with a missing id (src/AccountService.java:28-29) dereferences null at line 10 and throws NullPointerException, while an existing account owned by someone else throws SecurityException at line 15, so the two responses differ. The file has no controller, so whether these reach the client as distinct responses is not shown. Separately, deleteAccount (line 22) discards the canDelete result, so any authenticated user can delete a foreign account with no error, which is a more serious authorization flaw than the enumeration claim.
